slides.0.title: Gascony: Madiran, Saint-Mont and Armagnac
slides.0.subtitle: Home of Tannat, white wines and brandy
slides.1.title: Madiran
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The rules
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 10 July 1948; 37 communes; red only; Tannat at least 60% of each estate's vineyard; accessory varieties Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Fer (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Micro-oxygenation
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Patrick Ducournau of Domaine Mouréou found that controlled aeration softens rough tannins, usually between alcoholic and malolactic fermentation (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wikipedia and the INAO's 2025 specification both give about 1,300 ha
slides.1.content: Madiran is Tannat's most emblematic home.
slides.2.title: Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Dry white
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Courbu and Petit Manseng together at least 60% with neither above 80%; Sauvignon capped at 10%; residual sugar no more than 3 g/L (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Sweet white
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Hand-harvested with at least 12% potential alcohol and at least 35 g/L residual sugar (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Neighbours
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth's Gros Manseng page dates the Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh appellation to 1948
slides.2.content: On the same land, red is Madiran and white is Pacherenc.
slides.3.title: Saint-Mont and Tursan
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Saint-Mont
slides.3.highlights.0.content: AOC from 2011; about 1,200 ha in the Gers; a Benedictine monastery from the 11th century; the Plaimont cooperative groups about 1,000 growers; soils are clayey and pebbly in many colours
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Tursan
slides.3.highlights.1.content: VDQS in 1958 and AOC in 2011; about 450 ha; Baroque is 30–90% in whites; Tannat is capped at 40% in reds (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Location
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Tursan lies in the Landes and Gers, with the Adour as its northern boundary, next to Madiran on the east (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: Both were upgraded to AOC only in 2011, making them relatively young names.
slides.4.title: Côtes de Gascogne and Armagnac
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Côtes de Gascogne IGP
slides.4.highlights.0.content: About 12,000 ha with roughly 85% white; yield limit 120 hL/ha (Wine With Seth, INAO draft specification)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Armagnac distillation
slides.4.highlights.1.content: A single continuous distillation, leaving the still at 52–63% abv (cognac about 70%); aged in 400–420 L oak barrels and reduced to 40% for bottling (wein.plus)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Three zones
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Bas-Armagnac (west), Ténarèze (centre) and Haut-Armagnac (south and east); the main distilling grape is Ugni Blanc; Baco is a Folle Blanche × Noah hybrid (armagnac.fr)
slides.4.content: Armagnac area figures differ (about 12,000 or 20,000 ha), so they are not tested.
